summary: What runs at the end of the bonus build: Part 4's system plus player handles, moderated. A signed-in player saves a handle; the rules are checked first, then one Boolean question goes to a decision model through Vercel AI Gateway. A probability strictly above the threshold approves it, and anything else, including every failure, goes to a review queue that is a Postgres table. A new owner, the handles schema, publishes one view, handles.approved_v1, which the leaderboard view joins; nothing pending, in review or rejected reaches a page.

nodes.label: Reader
nodes.purpose: A blog reader exploring Bullpen's architecture timeline on the landing site.

nodes.label: Player
nodes.purpose: A visitor who sees live crypto and end-of-day stock prices and the leaderboard. Signing in with GitHub gives a player an account; the order ticket, the orders list showing the seven states, and the lifecycle behind them are built and tested.

nodes.label: Daily ingest cron
nodes.purpose: Vercel's scheduler: once a day after the U.S. close it calls the Market Data service's ingest, with a secret.

nodes.label: Bullpen Landing
nodes.purpose: The public landing site with the architecture timeline explorer.

nodes.label: Bullpen Trading App
nodes.purpose: The trading app. It owns orders and their lifecycle, reservations, fills, the ledger, positions and the leaderboard view in the trading schema, shows end-of-day stock prices read through prices_v1, signs players in with GitHub, lets a signed-in player set a handle and moderates it, and serves the authenticated sweep route the sweeper calls.

nodes.label: Market Data Service
nodes.purpose: Replaces the Price Snapshot Service: the CoinGecko price route moved into it. It owns both providers and both call budgets, and is the only writer of the market_data schema. A boundary in one release, not an independently deployed microservice.

nodes.label: CoinGecko
nodes.purpose: Crypto prices. Called only by the Market Data service, inside a monthly call budget, with the key in a header.

nodes.label: Alpha Vantage
nodes.purpose: U.S. stock prices, end of day, one request per symbol, fetched once a day by the Market Data service inside a daily call budget.

nodes.label: Google Analytics 4
nodes.purpose: Page views and a short list of events, only after the visitor accepts.

nodes.label: Microsoft Clarity
nodes.purpose: Heatmaps and session recordings, only after the visitor accepts.

nodes.label: trading schema
nodes.purpose: Accounts, orders with a state and a version, reservations, fills, order events, the ledger, positions and the leaderboard view. Every step of an order's life is one transaction here.

nodes.label: market_data schema
nodes.purpose: Quotes, the provider call ledger, and the view prices_v1.

nodes.label: market_data.prices_v1
nodes.purpose: The price contract: symbol, price, as-of time, source and a stale flag. The only thing outside market_data that trading may read.

nodes.label: Bullpen Database
nodes.purpose: One Neon project and one database, with a schema and a plain role per owner.

nodes.label: Sweeper
nodes.purpose: A daemon whose only job is to call the trading app's sweep route and wait: every 5 seconds while an order is open, backing off to every 60 minutes when none is. It reads no database URL and holds no data. Built and tested locally; declared in vercel.json, it runs in production deployments only.

nodes.label: Neon Auth
nodes.purpose: Neon's managed sign-in, enabled on the production branch with GitHub as its only provider. The trading app checks the access token it issues against its public keys and stores only the user's id.
nodes.costNote: Cost pending: not read from the console

nodes.label: handles schema
nodes.purpose: Schema handles, owned by the role handles_owner: one row per player's handle with its status and the model's probability, the review queue as a table, and the view approved_v1.

nodes.label: handles.approved_v1
nodes.purpose: The handle contract: owner user id and handle, for approved handles only. The only thing outside handles that trading may read, and the reason a pending, review or rejected handle cannot reach a page.

nodes.label: Vercel AI Gateway
nodes.purpose: Vercel's gateway to models, called once per new or changed handle with model typesafe-ai/jev: one Boolean question, is this handle acceptable to show publicly? Only the handle text is sent. A failure of any kind sends the handle to review; there is no fallback model.

steps.caption: Ask for a quote
steps.detail: The landing's price strip asks the trading app's domain for BTC-USD; a rewrite on /api/price sends the request to the Market Data service.

steps.caption: Fetch upstream
steps.detail: The service counts the call against its monthly budget, then calls CoinGecko server-side with the Demo API key in a header, never the URL.

steps.caption: Return the snapshot
steps.detail: Bullpen's own shape: symbol, price, changePercent, time, source, fetchedAt. The response says it varies by Origin.

steps.caption: Answer the strip
steps.detail: The allowed landing origin is echoed in the response, and nothing else is.

steps.caption: Read the price
steps.detail: Through prices_v1 only. A missing or stale price refuses the order and writes nothing; otherwise the order reserves buying power at a ceiling 5 % over that price.

steps.caption: Accept and reserve
steps.detail: One transaction: a conditional update reserves the buying power, then the order (accepted) and its reservation are inserted. A retry with the same client key returns the same order.

steps.caption: Book each fill
steps.detail: One transaction per fill, keyed by a unique fill id, so a second delivery changes nothing. A partial fill leaves the order partially filled; the order's version is checked on every update.

steps.caption: A cancel is requested, not done
steps.detail: The order stays open for fills until the venue confirms with an effective time; a fill executed before that time is booked even if it arrives after the order shows cancelled.

steps.caption: Find what is stuck
steps.detail: A pass that hands an unplaced order to the venue, cancels one with no fillable price, and releases what a finished order did not spend. Every step is idempotent, so a pass that dies is simply run again.

steps.caption: Save as pending
steps.detail: The rules are checked first (3 to 20 letters, digits, _ and -; unique ignoring case); a failing rule is a form error and no model is asked. Otherwise the handle is saved as pending, and the public label stays Player and four characters.

steps.caption: Ask one question
steps.detail: One Boolean question about the handle text, to typesafe-ai/jev, with a two second limit. Nothing else is sent: no user id, email, address or session.

steps.caption: Record the verdict
steps.detail: A probability strictly above the threshold approves the handle. Anything else, and every failure, puts it in the review queue, a table, with the probability for the reviewer.

steps.caption: Show it at the next refresh
steps.detail: The leaderboard view joins approved handles only, so a pending, review or rejected handle shows as the neutral label until a model or a person approves it.
